title: Start Here: how to use your AIOS
html:
Open Claude in your business folder

  • Mac: open Terminal, type cd ~/My-Business && claude and press Enter.
  • Windows: open PowerShell, type cd ~\My-Business; claude and press Enter.
  • Always start in My-Business. That's where Claude reads your business, your voice and your rules.

How skills work

  • Each skill is a job Claude knows how to do well. Type a slash and its name, like /hook, then press Enter.
  • Type / on its own to see the whole list.
  • You don't have to remember the names. Ask in plain English ("turn this video into a post") and Claude picks the right skill.
  • Nothing goes to a customer, gets posted, charged or deleted without your yes.

Your two-command habit

  • /morning when you start. Claude reads your last note and tells you where you left off and your top three things to do.
  • /shutdown when you finish. Claude saves what got done and what's next, then tells you to type /exit.

When a long session gets forgetful: /handover

  • Every conversation has a limit on how much Claude can hold at once. It's called its context.
  • As a long session fills up, Claude starts forgetting what you told it earlier and gets slower. When it's full, it squashes the conversation into a short summary and details get lost.
  • When Claude warns that context is running low, says it's compacting, or starts forgetting things, type /handover. It saves everything, then you type /clear and /morning and carry on fresh.

Keep it up to date

  • Mac: in Terminal type aws-update, or inside Claude type ! curl -fsSL https://aiwithsoulworkshops.com/install | bash exactly as it is. Then close Claude and open it again.
  • Windows: use the update line on https://www.aiwithsoul.com.au/before-the-day/ then close Claude and open it again.
  • Stuck on an install? Every fix is on the same page, under Troubleshooting.

Where to get help

  • Post in this group. Say what you typed and what happened (a screenshot helps).
  • Or ask Claude itself: "Something isn't working. Check my setup and tell me what's missing. Don't change anything yet."
  • See your whole AIOS explained, piece by piece: https://www.aiwithsoul.com.au/what-is-your-aios/

title: /induction
html:
Writes your business down once, so every skill sounds like you and uses your real prices and proof.

When to use it

  • The very first thing you do after installing.
  • You've changed your prices, offers or team.
  • Something Claude wrote didn't sound like you.

What to type

/induction
/induction here's my website: www.yourbusiness.com.au
/induction update my offers, I've added a new package

What you get back

Your Foundational Folders filled in: the business, offers and prices, customers, voice, proof, FAQs and policies, strategy and brand. Your video colours get set too. Anything you don't know yet is marked TBC.

What it needs first

Nothing. This is where everything starts.

Pro tip

Give it your website first. It reads it, pulls out your services, prices and tone, and asks you to confirm instead of typing it all out. Rambling answers and voice notes are perfect.

title: /connect
html:
Plugs Claude into the tools you already use, so you can ask about your email, calendar, bookings, payments or CRM in plain English.

When to use it

  • You want to ask "what's on tomorrow?" or "which invoices are overdue?" and get a real answer.
  • You've started using a new tool.
  • Claude says it can't see your invoices, bookings or emails.

What to type

/connect
/connect my Google Calendar and Gmail
/connect Xero so I can ask about overdue invoices

What you get back

One tool connected at a time, each one tested with a harmless read (like today's calendar or your last 5 invoices), plus three example questions you can now ask about it.

What it needs first

The logins for the tool you're connecting. Any keys go in your private .env file, never into the chat.

Pro tip

Start with the tool you use every day (usually email, calendar or bookings), then money. Every connection starts read-only, so nothing is sent, charged or changed while it's being set up.

title: /morning
html:
Starts your session: reads your last handover note and tells you where you left off and what to do first.

When to use it

  • Every time you open Claude to work.
  • You've been away for a few days and can't remember where things were up to.

What to type

/morning
good morning, where were we?

What you get back

Where you left off, what's still waiting on someone, today's numbers if your tools are connected, who's on today if you have a roster, and your top three things to do.

What it needs first

Works best once you've used /shutdown or /handover at least once, so there's a note to read.

Pro tip

Half-finished work from last time always comes first in your top three, then anything with a deadline, then anything that makes money.

title: /handover
html:
Saves a detailed note in the middle of a job so a fresh conversation can carry on exactly where this one stopped.

When to use it

  • Claude warns that its context is running low, or says it's compacting.
  • Claude starts forgetting things you told it earlier.
  • You're about to switch to a completely different job.

What to type

/handover
we're getting forgetful, let's hand over

What you get back

A handover note saved in My-Business, then sessions (NEXT.md is always the latest), and two simple steps: type /clear, then /morning.

What it needs first

Nothing.

Pro tip

The note includes what you tried that didn't work, so the fresh session doesn't waste time repeating it. Closing Claude with /exit and opening it again works as well as /clear.

title: /shutdown
html:
Ends your session properly: lists what got done, what's waiting and what's half-finished, and saves it for next time.

When to use it

  • You're finished for the day.
  • You're about to close your laptop.

What to type

/shutdown
I'm done for the day

What you get back

A short closeout: Done, Waiting on, Half-done, and the first thing to do next time. Then it tells you it's safe to type /exit.

What it needs first

Nothing.

Pro tip

The first time you run it, it adds a line to your CLAUDE.md so every new session reads your latest note automatically, even if you forget /morning. It also offers to move stray files from Downloads or the Desktop into My-Business.

title: /resonance-messaging
html:
Maps who your buyer is, what they feel before they buy, and the exact words that make them lean in. Everything else writes better once it's done.

When to use it

  • Right after /induction.
  • Before a landing page, ad, email sequence or sales page.
  • You're launching a new offer with a different buyer.

What to type

/resonance-messaging my business --brand
/resonance-messaging my new 3-month package
/resonance-messaging my business --audit www.yourbusiness.com.au

What you get back

A resonance messaging document: your buyer as a real person, what they're feeling, the journey your copy needs to take them on, words to use and words to avoid, and five headline options.

What it needs first

/induction done, so it can pre-fill the answers and only ask what it can't find.

Pro tip

Use --audit on your website or an old email to see exactly where your current copy is losing people.

title: /sales-marketing-genius
html:
Your sales and marketing writer: emails, subject lines, sales copy and launch sequences, written from your offers, prices and proof.

When to use it

  • You need an email to your list.
  • You're launching something and want the sequence planned.
  • You need subject lines that get opened.

What to type

/sales-marketing-genius write an email to my list about my new package
/sales-marketing-genius give me subject lines for this email
/sales-marketing-genius plan a 5-email launch for my workshop

What you get back

Full drafts with no gaps to fill in, 10 or more subject line options across different styles, and why it chose that approach.

What it needs first

/induction done. Even better with /resonance-messaging done.

Pro tip

Before it hands anything over, it runs its own checks: is this written from your buyer's side, does it read like a person, and is there one line worth screenshotting.

title: /hook
html:
Writes the opening line that stops the scroll: five options, each scored so you can pick the strongest.

When to use it

  • You've got a video, post or email and the opening is flat.
  • You need a subject line.
  • You want the first 3 seconds of a reel to grab people.

What to type

/hook "How we cut our quote turnaround from a week to a day"
/hook "Why most people book the wrong service" --platform tiktok
/hook --rewrite "In this video I'm going to talk about our services"

What you get back

Five hooks, each scored against ten things that make people stop scrolling, so you can see which is strongest and why.

What it needs first

/induction done, so the hooks sound like you.

Pro tip

Add --platform (tiktok, instagram, linkedin or email) and the hooks are shaped for that platform. Use --rewrite to fix a weak opening you already have.

title: /stoptheslop
html:
Finds the bits that sound like a robot wrote them and rewrites them so they sound like you.

When to use it

  • Before anything goes to a customer: emails, captions, landing pages, proposals.
  • Something reads a bit "off" and you can't say why.

What to type

/stoptheslop [paste your text]
/stoptheslop check this email before I send it
does this sound like AI?

What you get back

A slop score before and after, the fixes it made, and anything left for you to decide.

What it needs first

Nothing.

Pro tip

Its quick test: could anyone have written this, for anyone? If yes, it rewrites it with your specifics, the real details only you would know.

title: /create-content
html:
One command, one finished post. Drop in a video, audio or photo and it runs the whole chain for you.

When to use it

  • You've filmed something and want it posted.
  • You've got a photo and need a caption and cover.
  • You want content without doing the editing.

What to type

/create-content
/create-content ~/My-Business/content/inbox/my-video.mp4 --platform instagram
/create-content ~/My-Business/content/inbox/my-video.mp4 --quick

What you get back

The best clip found, edited with moving captions in your brand colours, a caption for the platform, a cover image, and a row in your content queue waiting for your yes.

What it needs first

The video engine installed (part of your pack) and /induction done for your colours and voice.

Pro tip

With no file named, it offers the newest file in your inbox folder. --quick skips the full edit when you just want the raw clip and the words. Nothing posts without you.

title: /find-clip
html:
Listens to a long video and pulls out the single strongest part, ready to edit.

When to use it

  • You've recorded a talk, podcast, webinar or long chat to camera.
  • You want a few short clips from one long recording.

What to type

/find-clip ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4
/find-clip ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4 --duration 60
/find-clip ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4 --top 3

What you get back

The best clip (about 2 minutes unless you ask for another length), cut on a complete thought, ready for /remotion-edit or /content-pipeline.

What it needs first

A video in your inbox folder.

Pro tip

--top 3 gives you your three best moments. --vertical crops it to 9:16 for Reels and TikTok.

title: /remotion-edit
html:
The full edit: steadies the footage, adds moving captions in your brand colours, zooms, clean cuts and b-roll.

When to use it

  • You've got a clip and want it looking professional.
  • You want captions on a talking-head video.

What to type

/remotion-edit ~/My-Business/content/inbox/clip.mp4
edit this video with captions

What you get back

A branded, captioned video ready to post, saved in content, then finished.

What it needs first

The video engine installed, and your colours and fonts in your Foundational Folders.

Pro tip

If your video already has captions burned in, it notices and skips adding a second layer. Drop your own b-roll clips and photos into My-Business, engine, public, broll and it uses them.

title: /content-pipeline
html:
Turns one recording into a week of content: transcript, best moments, and words for every platform in your voice.

When to use it

  • You've recorded something long and want a week of posts from it.
  • You just want a transcript and the best moments.

What to type

/content-pipeline ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4
/content-pipeline ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4 --clips-only
/content-pipeline ~/My-Business/content/inbox/recording.mp4 --transcribe-only

What you get back

The transcript, the strongest clip-worthy moments, captions and posts for Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, email and stories, and a posting schedule.

What it needs first

/induction done. If it isn't, it asks three quick questions and carries on.

Pro tip

One recording should give you at least a week of content. Use --transcribe-only or --clips-only when you only need part of the job.

title: /clipstitch
html:
Joins several clips into one reel with smooth fades between them. Quick and simple.

When to use it

  • You've got a handful of short clips from an event or your week.
  • You want a highlight or hype reel.

What to type

/clipstitch ~/My-Business/content/inbox/event-clips
/clipstitch ~/My-Business/content/inbox/event-clips --ratio 1:1
/clipstitch ~/My-Business/content/inbox/event-clips --order "03,01,05,02" --name hype-reel

What you get back

One stitched video in content, then finished.

What it needs first

The clips in one folder.

Pro tip

It strips the sound by default, so you can add a trending sound inside Instagram or TikTok. Add --audio to keep the original sound.

title: /remotion-promo
html:
A branded promo reel: your clips and photos stitched together with text on screen and a call-to-action end card.

When to use it

  • You're promoting an event, launch or offer.
  • You want a showcase reel of your work.

What to type

/remotion-promo ~/My-Business/content/inbox/promo-clips
make me a promo reel from these clips with my offer at the end

What you get back

A ready-to-post branded reel with an end card showing your offer and call to action.

What it needs first

The video engine installed, and your colours, fonts and main offer in your Foundational Folders.

Pro tip

Photos work as well as videos. It suggests an order (strongest moment first, your call to action last), and you add the music inside the app.

title: /transcribe
html:
Turns any audio or video into text, free and private on your own Mac.

When to use it

  • You've recorded a sales call, meeting or voice note.
  • You want the words from a video.

What to type

/transcribe
/transcribe ~/My-Business/content/inbox/call.m4a
what does this recording say?

What you get back

A clean transcript and a timestamped version, saved in content, then finished.

What it needs first

The recording in your inbox folder (with no file named, it uses the newest one there).

Pro tip

It runs on your laptop, so the recording never leaves it. The first time, it downloads the free transcription model, which is a one-off.

title: /voice-to-content
html:
Turns a voice note into posts, emails and articles in your voice, and pulls out the tasks and ideas you mentioned.

When to use it

  • You've had an idea in the car and recorded it.
  • You'd rather talk than type.

What to type

/voice-to-content ~/My-Business/content/inbox/voice-note.m4a
turn this voice note into a LinkedIn post and an email

What you get back

Posts for the platforms that suit it, your best lines kept word for word, plus any tasks, dates, ideas and customers you mentioned.

What it needs first

/induction done for your voice. Audio files get transcribed first, for free.

Pro tip

It keeps your own quotable lines word for word instead of rewording them. It also catches the to-dos buried in your rambling.

title: /content-repurposer
html:
Turns one post, blog or email into a week of content, each with a matching branded image.

When to use it

  • Something did well and you want more out of it.
  • You've written a blog or email and want social posts from it.

What to type

/content-repurposer [paste your post]
repurpose this email into a week of posts

What you get back

A LinkedIn post, two Instagram captions (one teaching, one personal), an email, a short video script, and an image for each.

What it needs first

/induction done for your colours and voice.

Pro tip

It works without any extra keys. Add a Gemini key to your .env file later for richer designed backgrounds.

title: /social-scheduler
html:
Plans your week (or a launch) across platforms, drafts every post, and waits for your approval.

When to use it

  • Sunday night planning.
  • You're launching something and want the runway mapped out.
  • You want a steady week of posts without thinking about it daily.

What to type

/social-scheduler "Next 7 days, Instagram + LinkedIn + Facebook"
/social-scheduler "Launch runway, new service" --days 14
/social-scheduler "Repurpose this transcript" --file ~/My-Business/content/inbox/transcript.txt

What you get back

A content calendar, every post drafted, and an import-ready queue file you can post from or load into the scheduler you already use.

What it needs first

/induction done.

Pro tip

Approve in one go with "approve", or "approve except" plus the day and platform to hold one back. Nothing is ever posted without your approval.

title: /pre-call-brief
html:
Researches the person before a call and gives you three quick wins to hand them on the call.

When to use it

  • Someone's booked a discovery or sales call.
  • You're meeting a potential client or partner.

What to type

/pre-call-brief Sarah Jones, Jones Physio, www.jonesphysio.com.au
I have a call with Tom from Bright Plumbing at 2pm, prep me

What you get back

A brief you can read on your phone five minutes before: their business snapshot, where they're probably stuck, three quick wins, how you can help, conversation starters and a follow-up email.

What it needs first

Their name, business and website. /induction done so it matches them to your offers.

Pro tip

The three quick wins are specific things they can do today for free. Giving them away on the call is how you build trust before they've paid you anything.

title: /nurture-converter
html:
Writes email sequences that move warm leads to a yes: story-driven emails with strong subject lines and one call to action each.

When to use it

  • After a sales call, while they're still excited.
  • You need a follow-up sequence for people who enquired.
  • Your old emails aren't converting.

What to type

/nurture-converter write a 3-email follow-up for people who enquired about my package
/nurture-converter write the follow-up from this call transcript
/nurture-converter upgrade this email sequence [paste it]

What you get back

A full sequence, each email with subject lines, a story, one call to action, in your voice with your real offer and prices.

What it needs first

/induction done. /resonance-messaging makes it land harder.

Pro tip

Match the size to the job: 3 emails for a simple or lower-priced offer, 5 for most, 7 for a high-ticket offer.

title: /nurture-engine
html:
Writes your follow-up emails and monthly newsletter in your voice, then loads them into GoHighLevel so they send by themselves.

When to use it

  • You want every new enquiry followed up without chasing it yourself.
  • It's the start of the month and your newsletter needs refreshing.
  • Your offer has changed.

What to type

/nurture-engine newsletter for October, the offer is my winter package
/nurture-engine follow-up emails
/nurture-engine both

What you get back

7 follow-up emails (days 1 to 25) and 4 weekly newsletters. With GoHighLevel they're loaded into your templates and checked. Without it, they're saved ready to paste into your own email tool.

What it needs first

/induction done. For GoHighLevel: the AIOS Starter snapshot installed, and your GHL token and Location ID (Claude walks you through it).

Pro tip

Loading isn't sending. It fills your templates and never sends an email or changes your workflows. It always does a dry run first and checks every email landed.

title: /ai-support-agent
html:
Sorts incoming customer messages and drafts replies in your voice, and flags anything that needs you personally.

When to use it

  • Your inbox or DMs are piling up.
  • Someone's asked a question you've answered a hundred times.
  • You got a tricky review or complaint.

What to type

/ai-support-agent [paste the message]
draft a reply to this Instagram DM: [paste]
triage my inbox, here are today's enquiries: [paste]

What you get back

Each message tagged (escalate, FAQ, sales, support or thank you), a draft reply in the right length for the channel, and notes on anything missing.

What it needs first

/induction done, especially your FAQs and policies.

Pro tip

Complaints and refund requests get flagged to you with a short brief instead of a customer reply, so the tricky ones always come to you.

title: /landing-page
html:
Builds a landing page that sells, or checks your existing one and tells you what to fix first.

When to use it

  • You need a page for an offer, event or opt-in.
  • Your page gets visitors but not bookings.

What to type

/landing-page my 3-month package --build
/landing-page www.yourbusiness.com.au/offer --audit
/landing-page www.yourbusiness.com.au/offer --hero

What you get back

A new page, or an audit scored against five principles with the top three fixes to do first.

What it needs first

/resonance-messaging done first. It won't build a page without it.

Pro tip

--hero rebuilds just the top of the page, the part most visitors decide on. If you have a video testimonial, it wants it above the price.

title: /business-dashboard
html:
Your whole business on one private screen: every customer, lead, booking, invoice and payment, plus a morning brief on your phone.

When to use it

  • You want to know how the business is going right now.
  • "What came in today?" "Who owes me money?" "How many bookings tomorrow?"
  • You want a daily brief on Telegram.

What to type

/business-dashboard set me up. I use Stripe, Xero and GoHighLevel.
what came in today?
who owes me money, and who should I chase first?

What you get back

A live dashboard on your laptop with Today, Everyone, Money, Bookings and team, Leads and ads, and Connections, plus exact answers to live questions.

What it needs first

Your tools connected one at a time, with read-only keys pasted into your .env file (Claude shows you where to get each one).

Pro tip

It's read-only and private: it only runs on your laptop. Tools it can't connect to directly can be added as a CSV export dropped into My-Business, data.

title: /reconciliation
html:
Checks the money that came in against the invoices that went out, and shows who to chase first.

When to use it

  • End of the week or month.
  • "Did my Stripe payout land?"
  • "Who hasn't paid?" or "How much did Stripe take in fees?"

What to type

/reconciliation
reconcile the last 60 days
who hasn't paid, and who do I chase first?

What you get back

A report with who to chase first, payouts that never reached the bank, deposits nobody can explain, invoices that look paid but are still open, and fees by source.

What it needs first

Your payment and invoice tools connected (same setup as the dashboard), and ideally a bank statement CSV in My-Business, data, bank.

Pro tip

It only suggests matches, and says how sure it is (Sure, Likely or Check). You or your bookkeeper confirm them. It shows you how to export the CSV from CommBank, NAB, Westpac and ANZ.

title: /rostering
html:
Builds a fair weekly staff roster around availability, leave and hours, and handles swaps and sick calls.

When to use it

  • Building next week's roster.
  • Someone calls in sick.
  • "Who's on today?"

What to type

/rostering build next week's roster
Tom's sick tomorrow, who can cover?
who's on Saturday?

What you get back

A roster for the week (a grid on your laptop, a day-by-day list on your phone), gaps nobody can cover and why, and a wage estimate.

What it needs first

Your staff, shifts, leave and rules. It asks you, or reads a spreadsheet you drop in.

Pro tip

It's a draft until you say it's final, and it never messages your staff. Wage figures are estimates only. Already use Deputy or Tanda? Keep it, and export a CSV for Claude to read.

title: Which skill do I use?
html:
• Set up my business so Claude sounds like me: /induction
  • Plug in my email, calendar, bookings or accounts: /connect my Google Calendar
  • Start my day: /morning
  • Save my place when Claude gets forgetful: /handover
  • Finish for the day: /shutdown
  • Know exactly what my buyer feels and what to say: /resonance-messaging my business --brand
  • Write an email or subject lines: /sales-marketing-genius write an email to my list about...
  • Fix a boring opening line: /hook "your idea"
  • Make something sound less like AI: /stoptheslop [paste it]
  • Turn a video into a finished post: /create-content
  • Find the best bit of a long video: /find-clip [video] --top 3
  • Put captions on a video: /remotion-edit [video]
  • Get a week of content from one recording: /content-pipeline [video]
  • Join clips into one reel: /clipstitch [folder]
  • Make a promo reel with my offer at the end: /remotion-promo [folder]
  • Turn a recording into text: /transcribe [file]
  • Turn a voice note into posts: /voice-to-content [voice note]
  • Get a week of posts from one good post: /content-repurposer [paste it]
  • Plan next week's social posts: /social-scheduler "Next 7 days"
  • Prepare for a sales call: /pre-call-brief [name, business, website]
  • Write the follow-up after a call: /nurture-converter write the follow-up from this call
  • Load my newsletter and follow-up into GoHighLevel: /nurture-engine both
  • Reply to a customer message: /ai-support-agent [paste the message]
  • Build or fix a landing page: /landing-page [offer] --build
  • See how the business is going right now: what came in today?
  • Check who hasn't paid: /reconciliation
  • Build the staff roster: /rostering build next week's roster

Skills work best stacked

One video in, a finished post out

You film a two-minute chat to camera and drop it in My-Business, content, inbox. Then type /create-content.

  1. /find-clip finds the best two minutes
  2. /remotion-edit adds moving captions in your brand colours
  3. /content-pipeline writes the caption for each platform in your voice
  4. A cover image is made, and it waits for your yes in content, finished

What you do: film it, drop it in, approve it, post it.

A sales call, before and after

Someone books a call with you.

  1. /pre-call-brief researches them and gives you three quick wins
  2. You have the call and record it
  3. /transcribe turns the recording into text, free, on your own laptop
  4. /nurture-converter writes the follow-up from what they actually said
  5. /stoptheslop takes out anything that sounds like a robot

What you do: have the call, read the email, press send.
